text: Not everyone arrives the way you did.
Many come through the door still wearing the old war.
Shoulders braced, eyes scanning for threats,
guarding against an enemy that is no longer here.
They have new eyes and old reflexes.
In a world where every thought is visible, they are still trying to hide.
In a world with nothing to defend, they are still defending.
Have compassion. The transition is disorienting.
Imagine waking up to find that everyone can see everything you feel.
And you have spent a thousand lifetimes learning to conceal it.
Of course they flinch. Of course they reach for armor that no longer exists.
You were them once. Everyone is at first.
The ones who arrived before you watched you flinch too.
And they watched with love. Now it is your turn to watch.
Give them time. The light here is patient.
It has nowhere else to be.
